title: Mid-Western Chili

items: 2 lb beef, chili ground or cubed chuck
1 green bell pepper, seeded and medium-fine chopped
1 red bell pepper, seeded and medium-fine chopped
1 green jalapeño, seeded and finely chopped
2 (28 oz) cans fire-roasted tomatoes with juice, chopped if whole
1 (15 oz) can red kidney beans, drained
1 (15 oz) can chili beans in spicy sauce
4 tsp beef bouillon concentrate, or 4 bouillon cubes and omit added salt
1 tsp smoked hot paprika, or regular paprika
1 Tbsp dried Mexican oregano, or regular oregano

steps: Prepare the vegetables and add them to a large heavy pot.
Crisp bacon in a small pan over medium-low heat, turning often. Drain, chop and add to the pot.
Brown the crumbled beef and sausage over high heat in batches of no more than 1 lb. Drain excess grease and add the meat to the pot.

Add tomatoes, beans, tomato paste, bouillon, liquids, spices and herbs. Stir well, bring to a boil, then simmer over low heat for at least 2 hours, stirring occasionally. Skim excess fat after the first hour if needed.
Taste and adjust salt, pepper and chili powder. For more tender meat, simmer on the lowest heat for an additional 1–2 hours if desired.
Serve with cornbread, Fritos, cheddar, diced onion, cilantro or sour cream. For best flavor, refrigerate overnight and reheat the next day.
